Implemented a general INI parser + printer for the `tonyfettes/ini` package, matching the dialect in `specs/ini.md`.

## What was built
- **`scanner.mbt`** — line splitting (LF/CRLF), blank trimming, raw trailing-backslash counting, and per-carrier escape decoding. Works on `StringView` slices so parsing copies only joined continuations and decoded values.
- **`parser.mbt`** — `pub fn parse`: single pass with a map cursor (`global` until the first header, then the current section's map; `Map` reference semantics make re-opening and last-wins fall out naturally). Role dispatch (blank / comment / section / entry), backslash-continuation joining, section-header parsing with quote stripping and nested-bracket rejection, first-`=`/`:` separator split, key validation (non-empty, no control chars), and value parsing (quoted vs unquoted, inline comments, escapes).
- **`printer.mbt`** — `pub fn print`: global entries then sections, always double-quoted values (escaping `\ " \n \r \t`), with quote-wrapping of section names only when needed. `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds.
- **`error.mbt`** — `IniError::InvalidSyntax(message)` for meaningful parse errors.
- **`ini_extra_test.mbt`** — 67 added edge-case tests (not one of the forbidden files).
- **`README.md`** — documents architecture, pipeline, escape table, printing, testing, and design decisions.

Notable rule decisions from the spec:
- Continuation is decided on the raw line *before* escapes (odd run = marker, even = literals).
- A value opening a quote is never continued (so unterminated quotes are rejected, never rescued by a later line).
- A continued value is treated as literal text — continuation lines' `=`, `:`, quotes and comment markers are ordinary characters.
- Inline comments start only at `;`/`#` directly preceded by a blank; quoted values suppress comment parsing.

- Whitespace trimming matches `String::trim`'s ASCII set, leaving Unicode whitespace as content.

## Key semantics (spec-driven, no fixture special-casing)

- First `=`/`:` splits key from value; key trimmed, verbatim (backslashes included), rejected if empty or holding a control char.
- Section name trimmed between `[`…`]`, rejected if empty or containing a bracket (`[]`, `[  ]`, `[[nested]]`, `[a]b`); one wrapping quote pair is dropped.
- Full-line comments and inline comments (`;`/`#` only after at least one blank, so `k=v;#x` keeps `;#x` and `k=#x` keeps `#x`).
- Quoted values close on the same line (backslash escapes the next char, so `\"` and `\'` cannot close), nothing but blanks/comment may follow; a quoted value never spans lines even behind a `\`.
- Continuation decided on the raw value text by counting the trailing backslash run **before** escape decoding — odd = marker (drop one, join next line directly, chains supported), even = escaped literals. Continued lines contribute text, not syntax; only the first line's `;`/`#` can be a comment.
- `parse` can never panic: every read goes through `Span::at`/`Span::sub` (clamped), verified by a 2000-case arbitrary-string property run.

### Key design points
- **Streaming**: every value is reassembled across partial reads; `read_into` loops until *n* bytes are held and raises on early EOF. Varints are read one byte at a time (no safe read-ahead). Length-delimited payloads are read in ≤4 KiB chunks into a growing buffer, so a bogus length cannot cause an out-of-memory panic.
- **Varints**: ≤10 bytes, non-minimal accepted, bits beyond the 64th dropped, 11th continuation an error; 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits, `int64`/`uint64` take all 64.

## Key correctness decisions
- **Streaming:** every value is reassembled across as many `read` calls as needed; EOF inside any value (key, varint, fixed width, payload, packed payload, group) raises.
- **Varints:** accept ≤10 bytes including non-minimal forms (`80 00` = 0); drop bits past the 64th (`80 ×9 7F` = 2^63); 11 bytes raises; 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits.

- **UTF-8** is delegated to `@utf8.decode(..., ignore_bom=false)`, which rejects overlong forms, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncations and stray continuations while keeping a leading U+FEFF.
- **Packed fields** decode through a `LimitedReader`; an empty payload is `[]` and a mid-element payload raises.
- **`read_unknown`** skips varint/8/len/4 bytes for wire types 0/1/2/5, skips groups recursively for wire type 3 (mismatched end tag or unterminated group raises), and raises for 4/6/7.
